recs.title: Answer-Distribution Trajectories: A Stochastic-Dynamics View of LLM Reasoning
recs.summary: This work introduces answer-distribution trajectories, a stochastic-dynamics-inspired representation that tracks the model's full predictive distribution over answers as reasoning unfolds, and suggests that answer-distribution trajectories provide a rich framework for analysing and evaluating the dynamics of LLM reasoning.

recs.title: RecurTrace: Adaptive Latent Reasoning with Loop-Time Memory
recs.summary: RecurTrace introduces Loop Memory Attention, which lets each looped layer attend to its own states from previous iterations along the loop-time axis, so the model can revisit earlier computations instead of relying on the latest state alone.

recs.title: Codebook Agent: Amortized Topology Design for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
recs.summary: Codebook Agent is the most accurate method on all six benchmarks the authors compare, and an MLP proxy that reads the flattened adjacency, regressed on measured utility and per-task normalized token cost, reranks the top decoded candidates in a single batched forward pass.

recs.title: Beneath the Diff: Diagnosing and Mitigating Algorithmic Mode Collapse in Code-Level Autonomous Research Loops
recs.summary: This work identifies a robust failure mode that is accompanied by a widening gap between in-loop metric gains and gains measured on independent held-out evaluations and proposes Diversity-Aware Proposal Sampling (DAPS), a lightweight mitigation that combines category-coverage reweighting, persistent edit memory, and a validation gate.

recs.title: From Atomic to Agentic: Towards Interpretable Evaluation of LLMs'Agentic Mathematical Capabilities
recs.summary: Experiments reveal that models with similar end-to-end accuracy can exhibit markedly different agentic capability profiles, demonstrating that process-level evaluation is crucial for interpreting the true potential of LLMs and guiding the development of next-generation mathematical agents.

recs.title: Prefix-Denoising Consistency: Test-Time Verification for Diffusion Language Models
recs.summary: PDC consistently improves upon the initial sample, outperforms independent generations under a computational constrained comparison, and is robust to different unmasking strategies and parameter settings, highlighting prefix-conditioned regeneration as an effective DLM-specific primitive for test-time verification.

recs.title: A survey on mathematical reasoning and optimization with large language models
RMA: an Agentic System for Research-Level Mathematical Problems
recs.summary: Through comprehensive expert evaluation, RMA outperforms strong baselines on the First Proof benchmark, including GPT-5.2R and Aletheia, solving eight out of ten research problems and producing more logically sound and readable proofs.

recs.title: FRAME: Learning the Adaptation Domain with a Mixture of Fractional-Fourier Experts
recs.summary: Fractional-Fourier Mixture of Experts improves over strong MoE-LoRA and spectral baselines -- including FlyLoRA, FourierMoE, and HMoRA -- while keeping the active-parameter budget small, and analysis shows that the learned orders specialize by task and layer in interpretable ways.

recs.title: The Routing Plateau: Understanding and Breaking the Accuracy Limits of LLM Routers
recs.summary: This investigation shows that the plateau is largely caused by a predictability bottleneck: current routers mainly learn global averaged model-performance trends rather than fine-grained query-specific routing signals, and that larger training datasets, stronger encoders, and end-to-end fine-tuning can further improve routing accuracy.

recs.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
recs.summary: This work recast the problem as selective trust and introduces MIST, a human-annotated benchmark that renders each reasoning item under four matched conditions, together with SC2W, a paired metric counting how often a misleading signal flips a clean-correct answer to wrong.

recs.title: Training Continuous Chain of Thought Models: A Tale of Two Regimes
recs.summary: C-MTP is introduced, a simpler, faster direct supervision approach that models each latent as an average of the embeddings in the CoT traces to be compressed, and outperforms a prior direct supervision method that approximates the distribution of compressed tokens.

recs.title: GSM-Plus-BN: A Perturbation-Based Benchmark for Bangla Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
recs.summary: This research makes a foundational contribution by providing GSM-PLUS-BN, a novel perturbated Bengali mathematical dataset derived from the English GSM-Plus benchmark, as a new resource and baseline for future Bengali mathematical reasoning research.

recs.title: BLADE: Scalable Bi-level Adaptive Data Selection for LLM Training
recs.summary: BLADE reformulates the bi-level optimization problem underlying influence-based methods as a penalized single-level objective via Lagrange multipliers, avoiding inverse-Hessian computation while revealing a principled connection to excess-loss based data selection.

recs.title: Artificial Intelligence for Mathematical Reasoning: An Integrated Survey of Language Models, Neuro-symbolic Systems, and Verified Discovery
recs.summary: This survey provides a unified account of the field's evolution, from early rule-based math word problem solvers and template-driven geometry systems, through neural expression generation and LLM prompting, to contemporary reasoning models, multi-agent systems, neuro-symbolic theorem provers, and verified discovery workflows.

recs.title: Minibatch Selection for Language Models via Partition Matroid Constrained Gradient Matching
recs.summary: PartitionSel, a cross-domain minibatch selection approach that maximizes a validation-guided gradient-matching utility under per-domain budgets encoded as a partition-matroid constraint, achieves robust gains over per-domain and domain-agnostic baselines on both benchmarks.

recs.title: Do NLP Models Know Numbers? Probing Numeracy in Embeddings
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: This work investigates the numerical reasoning capabilities of a state-of-the-art question answering model on the DROP dataset and finds this model excels on questions that require numerical reasoning, i.e., it already captures numeracy.

recs.title: Investigating the Limitations of Transformers with Simple Arithmetic Tasks
recs.summary: It is found that how a number is represented in its surface form has a strong influence on the model's accuracy, and this result bolsters evidence that subword tokenizers and positional encodings are components in current transformer designs that might need improvement.

recs.title: Exploring the Numerical Reasoning Capabilities of Language Models: A Comprehensive Analysis on Tabular Data
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: A hierarchical taxonomy for numerical reasoning skills with more than ten reasoning types across four levels: representation, number sense, manipulation, and complex reasoning is proposed.

recs.title: Number Cookbook: Number Understanding of Language Models and How to Improve It
recs.summary: This work introduces a benchmark covering four common numerical representations and 17 distinct numerical tasks in four major categories, and finetune practical-scale LLMs on proposed NUPA tasks and finds that naive finetuning can improve NUPA a lot on many but not all tasks, and surprisingly, techniques designed to enhance NUPA prove ineffective for finetuning pretrained models.

recs.title: Do Language Models Understand Measurements?
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: This study shows that PLMs lack the capability required for reasoning over measurements, and proposes a simple embedding strategy to better distinguish between numbers and units, which leads to a significant improvement in the probing tasks.

recs.title: Verb Physics: Relative Physical Knowledge of Actions and Objects
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: An approach to infer relative physical knowledge of actions and objects along five dimensions (e.g., size, weight, and strength) from unstructured natural language text is presented.

recs.title: Extracting Commonsense Properties from Embeddings with Limited Human Guidance
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This work proposes and assess methods for extracting one type of commonsense knowledge, object-property comparisons, from pre-trained embeddings and shows that an active learning approach that synthesizes common-sense queries can boost accuracy.

recs.title: Diversify Your Datasets: Analyzing Generalization via Controlled Variance in Adversarial Datasets
recs.venue: Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
recs.summary: This work extends the method to drive conclusions about a model’s ability to learn and generalize a target phenomenon rather than to “learn” a dataset, by controlling additional aspects in the adversarial datasets.

recs.title: Dissociating language and thought in large language models
